title: Windows/SolidWorks validation prep and docs
description:
## Context
All prior work is written and unit-tested without SolidWorks. This epic makes the eventual move to a Windows + SolidWorks machine turnkey: a self-contained smoke-test runner, generated sample geometry, Windows-marked integration tests, and user-facing docs.

## Success Criteria
- `scripts/validate_on_windows.py` produces a pass/fail report for every drawing tool
- Sample part + assembly generated by script (no binary fixtures in git)
- Integration tests marked `@pytest.mark.windows`, skipped off-Windows
- TOOLS.md reference + Windows setup guide

title: Add generated test geometry and Windows-marked integration tests
description:
## Context
Everything up to this point was written and unit-tested with no SolidWorks. The first real run happens on a Windows machine with SolidWorks installed. That session should be a single command that produces a verdict, not an interactive debugging expedition - so the geometry it needs must be generated by script, not shipped as binary fixtures in git.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- Add `scripts/make_test_geometry.py`: builds, from scratch using the EXISTING part/sketch/feature tools, (a) a bracket part with a rectangular base, several mounting holes, a fillet, and a chamfer, and (b) a two-component assembly using that part. Saves both under a `--out-dir` (default `tests/fixtures/generated/`, gitignored). Sets custom properties (PartNo, Description, Material, Revision) so title-block and BOM tools have something real to read.
- Add `solidworks_mcp/tests/integration/` with tests marked `@pytest.mark.windows` covering: create a drawing from template, add sheets, insert model/section/detail views, insert model items, add a dimension, add a note and a property note, add a GTOL and a datum, insert a BOM with balloons, insert a hole table, export PDF and DXF, and run one full `create_drawing_pack` from a `docs/packs/` example.
- These tests must be collected but skipped off-Windows (skip reason: "requires Windows + SolidWorks"), so `scripts/check.sh` stays green on macOS.
- Integration tests clean up after themselves: close documents without saving, delete files they created.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `scripts/make_test_geometry.py` is importable and passes a lint/compile check on macOS
- [ ] Integration tests are COLLECTED but SKIPPED on macOS with a clear skip reason
- [ ] `.venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -m windows` lists at least 12 tests
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` remains green on macOS
- [ ] Generated fixture output directory is gitignored
- [ ] Each integration test closes its documents and removes its files in a fixture teardown

## Verification
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --collect-only -m windows -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -m windows -q
.venv/bin/python -m compileall -q scripts/make_test_geometry.py
bash scripts/check.sh
```

title: Add scripts/validate_on_windows.py end-to-end validation runner
description:
## Context
The single command run on the Windows + SolidWorks machine. It exercises every registered drawing tool against real geometry and writes a report naming exactly which tools work, which fail, and with what COM error - turning the eventual porting session into a triage list rather than a debugging session.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- Add `scripts/validate_on_windows.py`. It must: refuse to run off Windows with a clear message; connect to SolidWorks and print the detected version against the configured minimum; generate the test geometry via `scripts/make_test_geometry.py`; then invoke EVERY registered tool at least once with sensible arguments derived from the registry.
- Tools that cannot be auto-exercised (they need a specific selection or prior state) get an explicit, named exclusion list in the script with a stated reason - never a silent skip.
- Never abort on failure: catch per-tool, record the exception and any COM HRESULT, and continue. One broken tool must not hide the status of the other forty.
- Write `validation_report.md` and `validation_report.json` to the output dir: per tool the status (pass/fail/skipped), the arguments used, the result message, and the elapsed time. End with a summary table and a nonzero exit code if anything failed.
- Add `--only <pattern>` and `--skip <pattern>` so a follow-up run can re-test just the failures.
- Leave SolidWorks in a clean state on exit: close every document it opened without saving, even on an exception.
- Run in a headless-ish mode where possible: suppress dialogs via the documented user preferences, and restore them afterwards.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Running on macOS prints a clear "requires Windows" message and exits nonzero without connecting
- [ ] The script enumerates tools from the registry rather than a hardcoded list, so new tools are covered automatically
- [ ] A tool raising an exception is recorded and the run continues
- [ ] Both report files are written, and the JSON report has one entry per registered tool
- [ ] The exclusion list is explicit, with a reason string per excluded tool
- [ ] `--only` and `--skip` filter correctly (unit-tested on macOS with a fake registry)
- [ ] `solidworks_mcp/tests/test_validation_runner.py` covers filtering, report generation, and the failure-continues behaviour without SolidWorks
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

## Verification
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest solidworks_mcp/tests/test_validation_runner.py -q
.venv/bin/python scripts/validate_on_windows.py; echo "exit=$? (expected nonzero on macOS)"
bash scripts/check.sh
```

title: Add insert_model_items tool (import model annotations)
description:
## Context
When a part was modeled with design intent (DimXpert or driving dimensions), pulling those annotations onto the drawing is by far the fastest route to a fully dimensioned view. `IView::InsertModelAnnotations3` and the document-wide `IModelDocExtension::InsertModelAnnotations3` per `docs/api/03-annotations.md`.

## Requirements
- `insert_model_items(view_name=None, sources=None, types=None, all_views=False, eliminate_duplicates=True, hidden_features=False)`.
- `types` selects what to import: dimensions, datums, gtols, surface finishes, weld symbols, notes, hole callouts, center marks, centerlines. Combine into the option bitmask documented in the dossier; default to dimensions + hole callouts + center marks.
- `sources` selects where they come from: the whole model, a selected feature, or DimXpert; map to the documented source enum.

title: Add dimension, ordinate dimension, and autodimension tools
description:

Fallback dimensioning for anything DimXpert did not capture: drawing-only reference dimensions between picked entities, ordinate dimensions, and a bulk autodimension pass. Per `docs/api/03-annotations.md`.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)

## Requirements
- `add_dimension(view_name, entities, x, y, dimension_type="smart")` - `entities` is a list of entity references (as returned by `list_view_entities` from the selection primitive). Select them atomically, then call the documented dimension API. Types: smart, horizontal, vertical, radial, diameter, angular. Return the created dimension's name and its value in user units.
- `add_ordinate_dimensions(view_name, origin_entity, entities, x, y, direction="horizontal")` - baseline/ordinate chain from a datum origin.
- `set_dimension_value(dimension_name, value)` / `set_dimension_text(dimension_name, prefix=None, suffix=None, override=None)` - for tolerance callouts and "TYP"/"REF" annotations.
- `autodimension_view(view_name, scheme="baseline", entities="all", horizontal_placement="above", vertical_placement="left")` - the autodimension family; a "just add reasonable baseline dimensions" fallback when the model carries no DimXpert data. If the dossier concluded no usable autodimension API exists for this SolidWorks version, record that in the dossier and return a clear unsupported error from the tool instead of a stub that pretends to work.
- Every dimension value crossing the tool boundary is in user units; the API is meters.

- [ ] `set_dimension_value` converts user units to meters at the boundary

title: Add GD&T feature control frame and datum tools
description:
## Context
Geometric tolerancing on structural connection points is exactly what a certification reviewer or PE re-stamping the package will check, so this is a load-bearing capability rather than a nice-to-have. `IModelDocExtension::CreateGTOL`, `CreateDatumTag`, and `CreateDatumTargetSym` per `docs/api/03-annotations.md`.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- `add_datum_feature(view_name, entity, label, x, y, style=None)` - place a datum tag (A, B, C...) on a selected edge/face/dimension. Auto-assign the next unused letter when `label` is omitted, by reading existing datum tags on the sheet.
- `add_gtol(view_name, entity, symbol, tolerance, datums=None, x=None, y=None, material_condition=None, projected_zone=None, leader=True)` - feature control frame. `symbol` covers the 14 geometric characteristics (position, flatness, perpendicularity, parallelism, concentricity, straightness, circularity, cylindricity, profile of a line, profile of a surface, angularity, symmetry, circular runout, total runout). `datums` is an ordered list of up to 3 datum references, each optionally with a material-condition modifier (MMC/LMC/RFS).
- Build the frame-content string using the syntax documented in the dossier and validate it before calling COM: a position tolerance without a datum reference, or a datum letter that does not exist on the drawing, must error rather than produce a meaningless frame.
- `add_datum_target(view_name, entity, label, area_type, size, x, y)` - datum target symbol.
- `list_datums(sheet_name=None)` - enumerate existing datum tags so `add_gtol` validation and auto-lettering have something to read.
- Include a compound-frame case: composite feature control frames (two stacked rows).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All 14 geometric characteristic symbols map to the dossier-documented enum/string values
- [ ] The frame-content string is asserted byte-for-byte against the call log for at least 4 cases including a composite frame
- [ ] A GTOL referencing a datum letter absent from the drawing errors with `swInvalidInput`
- [ ] Auto-lettering picks the next unused letter and skips the reserved letters I, O, Q
- [ ] MMC/LMC/RFS modifiers appear in the right position within the frame

## Requirements
- `insert_model_view(model_path, view_name="*Front", x=0, y=0, sheet_name=None)` - wraps `CreateDrawViewFromModelView3(ModelName, ViewName, X, Y, Z)`. Accept the friendly names Front/Top/Right/Left/Bottom/Back/Isometric/Dimetric/Trimetric/Current and map them to the `*Name` form SolidWorks expects. ## Context

It is also a prime `ComSignature` typed-wrapper candidate. Follow `docs/api/02-views.md`.

- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- `insert_section_view(parent_view_name, cut_points, x, y, label=None, flip_direction=False, section_type="full", auto_hatch=True, display_only=False, use_sheet_scale=True)`.
- `cut_points` is a list of 2+ (x, y) pairs in the parent view's coordinate space, in user units. Two points is a straight cut; more points is an offset/stepped section. Validate that at least two distinct points are supplied before touching COM.
- The tool must handle the whole sequence internally: activate the parent view, create the cut-line sketch segments via the sketch manager, select them, call `CreateSectionViewAt5`, then close/clean up. The caller never manages sketch or selection state.
- `section_type` covers full / half / aligned per the enum captured in the dossier; reject an unsupported combination (for example half-section with more than two cut points) with `swInvalidInput`.
- If SolidWorks pops a section-scope dialog for assemblies, note the mitigation found during research in the tool description and set `ISldWorks::SetUserPreferenceToggle` accordingly, restoring it afterwards.
- Return the created section view's name and its label letter.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Cut-line coordinates reach COM in meters
- [ ] Fewer than 2 points, or 2 identical points, returns `swInvalidInput` with no COM call
- [ ] Offset sections with 3+ points produce the right number of sketch segments

title: Add view placement, alignment, display, and deletion tools
description:
## Context
A batch-generated pack that leaves views overlapping is unusable. These tools control placement, alignment, per-view scale and display mode, and deletion so a pack can be regenerated without restarting the document. Follow `docs/api/02-views.md`.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- `move_view(view_name, x, y)` - `IView::Position`. Note that projected views are alignment-locked to their parent; detect that case and report it rather than silently no-op'ing.
- `align_view(view_name, reference_view_name, alignment)` - horizontal/vertical/by-origin per the alignment enum; also expose breaking alignment so a locked view can be moved freely.
- `set_view_scale(view_name, scale_num=None, scale_denom=None, use_sheet_scale=False)` - per-view scale independent of the sheet scale.
- `set_view_display_mode(view_name, mode, shadows=False, high_quality=True)` - `IView::SetDisplayMode3`; mode is wireframe / hidden-lines-visible / hidden-lines-removed / shaded / shaded-with-edges.
- `delete_view(view_name)` - `DeleteView2`, refusing to delete a view that has dependent child views unless `cascade=True` is passed, in which case delete children first and report what was removed.
- `auto_arrange_views(sheet_name=None, margin=None)` - a composite that reads every view's bounding box (`IView::GetOutline`) and lays views out on the sheet without overlap. This is the tool that makes a generated pack presentable; keep the algorithm simple and deterministic (row packing, respecting existing parent-child alignment) and document it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 6 tools registered and dispatchable
- [ ] `move_view` on an alignment-locked view reports the lock instead of silently failing
- [ ] `delete_view` refuses a parent with children unless `cascade=True`, and reports every view it removed
- [ ] `auto_arrange_views` is deterministic - the same input view outlines always yield the same positions (asserted twice in one test)
- [ ] `auto_arrange_views` produces no overlapping bounding boxes for a 6-view fixture

title: Add DrawingOperations mixin and typed COM parameter wrapper
description:
## Context
`SolidWorksAutomation` is composed from mixins in `solidworks_mcp/automation/__init__.py`. Drawing work needs its own mixin plus a mechanism for the parameter-heavy COM calls: `SetupSheet5`, `CreateSectionViewAt5`, and `InsertBomTable3` all take 10+ positional arguments, and passing those positionally from tool code is where parameter-order bugs live.

## Requirements
- Create `solidworks_mcp/automation/drawings.py` with a `DrawingOperations` mixin following the existing mixin contract documented in `solidworks_mcp/automation/documents.py` (uses `self._sw_app`, `self.is_connected`, `self.connect()`, `self._result()`, `self._units`).
- Mix it into `SolidWorksAutomation` in `solidworks_mcp/automation/__init__.py` and update that class docstring.
- Add `get_drawing_doc(self) -> Tuple[Any, Optional[Dict]]`: like the existing `get_active_doc`, but also verifies `IModelDoc2::GetType == swDocDRAWING` and returns a clear error otherwise. Handle the property-vs-method ambiguity the same way `base.py::_get_doc_title` does.
- Create `solidworks_mcp/automation/com_params.py` with a `ComSignature` helper: declare a method name and an ordered list of `Param(name, default, converter)`, then call `sig.bind(**kwargs) -> tuple` producing the positional args. Converters cover the common cases: identity, `to_meters`, `to_radians`, enum-to-int, and bool.
- `ComSignature.bind` must raise a descriptive error on an unknown keyword and fill defaults for omitted ones - so a typo in a tool becomes a test failure, not a silently-wrong COM call.
- Add `sig.describe()` returning a JSON-schema-shaped dict of the named params, so MCP tool schemas can be generated from the same declaration.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `DrawingOperations` is part of `SolidWorksAutomation`s MRO
- [ ] `get_drawing_doc` returns an error result (not an exception) when the active doc is a part
- [ ] `ComSignature.bind` produces the exact positional tuple, applies converters, and rejects unknown kwargs
- [ ] `ComSignature.describe()` output is valid for use as an MCP `inputSchema` properties block
- [ ] `solidworks_mcp/tests/test_com_params.py` covers bind ordering, defaults, unit conversion, and the unknown-kwarg error
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

title: Add selection primitive and atomic select-then-act helper
description:
## Context
Almost every annotation call and many view-editing calls act on whatever is currently selected via `ISelectionMgr`, not on an object reference passed in. Making the LLM manage selection across tool calls means stale-selection bugs. The decision for this project: every annotation tool selects and acts atomically server-side, and `select_entity` is exposed only as an escape hatch.

## Requirements
- Add to `solidworks_mcp/automation/drawings.py` (or a sibling `selection.py` mixin):
  - `select_by_id(name, type_str, x, y, z, append=False, mark=0, callout=None, sel_option=0) -> Dict` wrapping `IModelDocExtension::SelectByID2` per `docs/api/03-annotations.md`.
  - `clear_selection() -> Dict` wrapping `IModelDoc2::ClearSelection2`.
  - `get_selection_info() -> Dict` reporting count and each selected object type via `ISelectionMgr`.
  - `select_view_by_name(view_name) -> Dict` - resolve an `IView` by name and select/activate it; this is the target of most drawing operations.
  - `list_view_entities(view_name) -> Dict` - enumerate pickable entities in a view (edges, vertices, faces) with their sheet-space coordinates, so an LLM can pick an annotation target without a mouse.
- Add a `selected(...)` context manager that clears selection, performs the selection, yields, and clears again on exit including on exception. Every annotation tool must use it.
- Selection failure must return a structured error result using `SwErrors.swSelectionError`, never raise.
- Record what was selected in the result `data` so tool output is self-explaining.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `select_by_id` passes arguments to `SelectByID2` in the exact order documented in `docs/api/03-annotations.md`, asserted against the fake-COM call log
- [ ] The `selected(...)` context manager clears selection on both the success and the exception path
- [ ] `select_view_by_name` returns a clear error for an unknown view name
- [ ] `list_view_entities` returns coordinates in the units set by `set_units`, not raw meters

title: Refactor server.py to a declarative tool registry
description:
## Context
`solidworks_mcp/server.py` lists 25 tools in `list_tools()` and dispatches them through a ~160-line `if/elif` chain in `call_tool()`. This project adds roughly 45 more tools. Without a registry, every new tool means editing two distant places and the two lists drift (see the parity test added in the harness epic).

## Requirements
- Add `solidworks_mcp/tools/registry.py` with a `@tool(name, description, schema)` decorator that registers a handler function into an ordered registry, and `build_tool_list()` / `dispatch(name, arguments)` helpers.
- Handlers take the raw `arguments` dict and return the existing standard result dict, so `format_result` in `server.py` is unchanged.
- Schemas may be supplied literally or generated from a `ComSignature.describe()` (from the infra epic) - support both.
- Migrate ALL existing tools in `solidworks_mcp/server.py` into `solidworks_mcp/tools/` modules grouped by area: `connection.py`, `documents.py`, `sketches.py`, `features.py`, `utility.py`. Behaviour must be identical - the existing tool names, descriptions, defaults, and result text stay byte-identical.
- `server.py::list_tools` becomes `return build_tool_list()`; `call_tool` becomes a try/except around `dispatch(...)` keeping the existing logging and error formatting.
- Keep `_execute_python_fixed`, `_list_features_fixed`, `_close_sketch_handler`, `_get_sketch_status_handler` working - move them into the appropriate tools module rather than deleting them.
- Registering two tools with the same name must raise at import time.

The drawing-pack workflow needs document plumbing beyond what `solidworks_mcp/automation/documents.py` has today: creating a drawing from a `.drwdot` template, telling part/assembly/drawing apart, forcing rebuilds between phases, decoding save errors, and reading/writing the custom properties that drive title blocks.

## Requirements
Implement as registered tools (using the registry from the infra epic) backed by `DrawingOperations`:
- `new_drawing_from_template(template_path=None, paper_size="A3", orientation="landscape", scale_num=1, scale_denom=1)` - `ISldWorks::NewDocument`. When `template_path` is omitted, reuse `solidworks_mcp/utils/sw_finder.py::find_template` to locate a `.drwdot`; return a clear `swTemplateNotFound` error if none is found. Return the new documents title and sheet name.
- `get_document_type()` - `IModelDoc2::GetType` mapped to a readable name via `SwDocumentTypes`.
- `open_or_activate_document(filepath, read_only=False, lightweight=False)` - `OpenDoc6` if not already open, else `ActivateDoc3`; expose the lightweight/resolved option since large assemblies feed these drawings.
- `rebuild_document(force=True, top_level_only=False)` - `ForceRebuild3` / `EditRebuild3`.
- `save_drawing(filepath=None)` - `Save3`/`SaveAs3` capturing the errors/warnings byref outputs and decoding them with `decode_save_error`; a nonzero error must produce `success=False`, not a silent pass.
- `get_custom_properties(configuration=None)` / `set_custom_properties(properties: dict, configuration=None)` - via `IModelDocExtension::CustomPropertyManager`, per `docs/api/01-documents-and-sheets.md`.

- [ ] `new_drawing_from_template` falls back to template discovery and errors clearly when none exists

title: Establish docs/api dossier format, index, and validator
description:
## Context
The research issues in this epic each produce a document under `docs/api/`. Implementation issues later read those documents instead of guessing COM signatures. This issue defines the format once and makes completeness machine-checkable, so later research issues can be verified without a human reading them.

## How to research (no SolidWorks on this machine)
Use WebFetch/WebSearch against the official API help. Canonical URL shape:
`https://help.solidworks.com/2025/english/api/sldworksapi/SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks~SolidWorks.Interop.sldworks.<Interface>~<Method>.html`
Enum pages: `https://help.solidworks.com/2025/english/api/swconst/SolidWorks.Interop.swconst~SolidWorks.Interop.swconst.<enum>_e.html`
Also useful: the CodeStack API reference (codestack.net), and the SolidWorks API forum for known parameter-order gotchas. Cross-check every signature against at least two sources when the help page is ambiguous, and say so in the doc.
If a page cannot be fetched, record the method with `status: unverified` and an explicit note - never invent a signature.

## Requirements
- Create `docs/api/README.md`: states the target release (SolidWorks 2025), the URL patterns above, the units convention (SolidWorks API is meters and radians everywhere), and an index table of dossier files with their status.
- Create `docs/api/_TEMPLATE.md` demonstrating the record format below with one fully worked example: `IDrawingDoc::NewSheet4`. Fetch that page for real - the example must be accurate.
- Create `scripts/check_api_docs.py`: parses every `docs/api/*.md` except README/_TEMPLATE and fails (exit 1) if a file is missing the required sections, if any method record lacks a Signature / Parameter table / Source URL / status line, or if a file has fewer method records than the `min_methods:` count declared in its own YAML front matter.
- Wire `scripts/check_api_docs.py` into `scripts/check.sh` so dossier rot breaks the build.

## Required per-method record format
Each documented method gets an H3 heading and this table plus notes:
- **Interface** / **Method** / **Minimum SW version**
- **Signature** - full ordered parameter list with COM types
- **Parameter table** - name | type | units (meters/radians!) | required | meaning | enum ref
- **Returns** - type and what a failure looks like (None / False / 0 / negative code)
- **Prior selection required** - what must be selected via ISelectionMgr before the call, or "none"
- **Source URL(s)**
- **status:** verified | unverified
- **Gotchas** - deprecated predecessors, parameter-order traps, dialog-popping risk

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `docs/api/README.md` and `docs/api/_TEMPLATE.md` exist
- [ ] The NewSheet4 example carries a real, fetched source URL and its true parameter order
- [ ] `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_api_docs.py` exits 0 on the current tree
- [ ] The validator exits 1 when a required section is deleted from a doc (prove it with a temp file in a test)
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` invokes the validator
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

## Verification
```bash
.venv/bin/python scripts/check_api_docs.py; echo "exit=$?"
.venv/bin/python -m pytest solidworks_mcp/tests/test_api_docs_validator.py -q
bash scripts/check.sh
```

title: Add PDF export tool with save-error decoding
description:
## Context
PDF is the shop-floor-facing deliverable. `IModelDocExtension::SaveAs3` with `IExportPdfData` for sheet selection, per `docs/api/05-export-and-layers.md`. Save failures on drawings are common (read-only sheet, rebuild errors, missing references) so error decoding matters more here than anywhere else.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- `export_pdf(output_path, sheets="all", open_after=False, keep_invisible_layers=False, high_quality=True)` - `sheets` is "all", "current", or an explicit list of sheet names. Build `IExportPdfData` via `ISldWorks::GetExportFileData`, set the sheet list, then `SaveAs3`.
- Capture the byref errors/warnings outputs and decode them with `decode_save_error`; a nonzero error code must yield `success=False` with the decoded text in the message.
- Create the output directory if it does not exist; error clearly if the path is not writable or the file is locked (a PDF open in a viewer is the single most common real-world failure).
- Verify the file actually exists on disk after the call and include its size in `data`. A COM call that returns True but writes no file is a real failure mode.
- Name every sheet that was exported in the result `data`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `sheets="all"`, `"current"`, and an explicit list all set the export data correctly, asserted in the call log
- [ ] A nonzero save-error code produces `success=False` with decoded text
- [ ] A missing output file after a "successful" COM call produces `success=False`
- [ ] The output directory is created when absent
- [ ] An unknown sheet name in the explicit list errors before touching COM, listing available sheets
- [ ] `solidworks_mcp/tests/test_tools_export_pdf.py` has at least 12 tests
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

title: Build recording fake-COM harness for SolidWorks objects
description:
## Context
Every drawing tool in this project will be written on a machine with no SolidWorks. The only way to verify a tool autonomously is to assert on the exact COM calls it makes: method name, positional argument order, and argument values (especially unit conversion to meters). This issue builds that harness.

## Requirements
- Create `solidworks_mcp/testing/fake_com.py` (new `testing` package, shipped with the library so the Windows machine can use it too).
- Implement `FakeComObject`: records every attribute access and every call as `Call(path, name, args, kwargs)` onto a shared `CallLog`. Unknown attributes auto-vivify into child `FakeComObject`s so deep chains like `doc.SketchManager.InsertSketch(True)` work without pre-declaration.
- Support the property-vs-method ambiguity the existing code deals with (see `server.py::_list_features_fixed`): a fake attribute must be usable BOTH as a value and as a callable, so `feat.GetTypeName2` and `feat.GetTypeName2()` both work.
- Support scripted return values: `fake.set_return("IDrawingDoc.CreateDrawViewFromModelView3", view_obj)` and `set_sequence(...)` for successive calls.
- Support scripted failures: `fake.set_raises(path, exception)` and returning `None`/`False` to exercise the error paths every tool must handle.
- Provide `FakeSldWorks` factory building a plausible object graph: app -> ActiveDoc (Part/Assembly/Drawing) with `GetType`, `Extension`, `SelectionManager`, `FeatureManager`, `SketchManager`, and for drawings `GetCurrentSheet`, `GetSheetNames`, `IGetViews`.
- Provide `CallLog` query helpers: `calls_to(name)`, `assert_called_with(name, *args)`, `arg_of(name, index)`, `ordered_names()`.
- Document the harness in a module docstring with a copy-pasteable example.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `solidworks_mcp/testing/fake_com.py` exists and imports with no pywin32
- [ ] Attribute chains auto-vivify; `x.Foo` and `x.Foo()` both work on the same attribute
- [ ] `set_return`, `set_sequence`, and `set_raises` all covered by tests in `solidworks_mcp/tests/test_fake_com.py`
- [ ] `CallLog` records positional args in order and exposes them for assertion
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

## Verification

```bash
bash scripts/check.sh
```

title: Define declarative drawing-pack spec and validator
description:
## Context
Rather than exposing every primitive and hoping the LLM sequences 15-20 calls correctly per part, the pack is described declaratively and a deterministic compiler lowers it into ordered SolidWorks calls. This issue defines that spec and its validator - no COM calls at all, so it is fully testable here.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- Create `solidworks_mcp/pack/spec.py` with dataclasses describing a pack: `PackSpec(drawing_template, output, sheets=[SheetSpec])`; `SheetSpec(name, model_path, paper_size, scale, views=[ViewSpec], annotations=[AnnotationSpec], tables=[TableSpec], properties={})`; `ViewSpec` covering every view kind from the view epic (model, projected, section, detail, broken-out, break, crop) with a discriminating `kind` field; `AnnotationSpec` and `TableSpec` likewise.
- `PackSpec.from_dict` / `to_dict` for JSON round-tripping, and `PackSpec.from_json_file`.
- `validate() -> list[str]` returning human-readable problems WITHOUT touching COM: unknown view kind, a section/detail view naming a parent that is not defined earlier in the same sheet, duplicate view names, duplicate sheet names, an annotation targeting an undefined view, a GTOL referencing an undefined datum, a balloon spec with no BOM on the sheet, a missing required field.
- Emit a JSON Schema for the spec (`solidworks_mcp/pack/schema.json`) generated from the dataclasses, so the MCP tool schema and the docs stay in sync with the code.
- Include 3 worked example specs under `docs/packs/`: a single-part pack, an assembly pack with BOM and balloons, and a multi-sheet pack with a section and a detail view. Each must pass `validate()` in a test.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `PackSpec` round-trips through `to_dict`/`from_dict` losslessly for all 3 examples
- [ ] `validate()` catches every listed error class - one test per class, at least 9 tests
- [ ] `validate()` returns an empty list for all 3 example packs
- [ ] `schema.json` is generated from the dataclasses (not hand-written) and is valid JSON Schema

title: Add pack compiler and create_drawing_pack composite tool
description:
## Context
The compiler that turns a validated `PackSpec` into an ordered sequence of primitive calls, plus the `create_drawing_pack` MCP tool that runs it. Rebuild timing is a correctness requirement here, not a nicety: dimension values, BOM quantities, and balloon numbers stay stale until a rebuild, so the compiler must rebuild between the view phase and the annotation phase - not only at the end.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- Create `solidworks_mcp/pack/compiler.py` with `compile(spec) -> list[Step]` where each `Step` names a registered tool and its arguments. Compilation is pure - no COM, fully unit-testable.
- Enforce the phase order per sheet: create sheet -> set sheet properties -> insert views (parents before children) -> auto-arrange -> REBUILD -> insert model items and annotations -> insert tables -> REBUILD -> update tables -> balloons -> set custom properties -> export.
- Add `create_drawing_pack(spec)` as a registered MCP tool: validate, compile, then execute steps via the tool registry, collecting a per-step result. On a step failure, respect a `on_error` policy of `"abort"` (default) or `"continue"`, and always return the full step log so a partial pack is diagnosable.
- Add `dry_run=True` to return the compiled step list without executing - this is how the pack can be reviewed before it touches a real SolidWorks session.
- Return a summary: sheets created, views inserted, annotations added, tables added, files exported, and every failure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `compile()` emits rebuild steps in both required positions, asserted by index in the step list
- [ ] Parent views are always compiled before views that reference them, including when the spec lists them out of order
- [ ] `compile()` makes no COM calls (asserted with an empty fake call log)
- [ ] `dry_run=True` returns the step list and executes nothing
- [ ] `on_error="abort"` stops at the first failure; `on_error="continue"` runs the rest and reports both
- [ ] All 3 example packs from the spec issue compile without error
- [ ] `solidworks_mcp/tests/test_pack_compiler.py` has at least 14 tests
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

## Verification


title: Add SolidWorks version gating and generated tool index
description:
## Context
SolidWorks method signatures drift across releases (CreateDrawViewFromModelView -> ...3, InsertBomTable -> ...3/4). Silently calling a deprecated overload produces confusing runtime behaviour on someone else's install. This project targets SolidWorks 2025 as the minimum; that decision needs enforcement in code, and the whole tool surface needs a discoverable index.

## Working agreement (applies to every tool issue)
- Signatures and parameter order come from the `docs/api/` dossier. If the dossier lacks something, fetch the help.solidworks.com page and ADD it to the dossier as part of this issue rather than guessing.
- Implement the automation method on the `DrawingOperations` mixin, register the MCP tool via the `@tool` registry, and use `ComSignature` for any COM call with more than 6 parameters.
- Public tool API takes lengths in the user unit (`set_units`) and angles in degrees; convert to meters/radians at the COM boundary via `self._units`.
- Never raise out of a tool - return the standard result dict with the right `SwErrors` code.
- Annotation/view operations that depend on selection must use the `selected(...)` context manager so selection is atomic server-side.
- Tests use the fake-COM harness and assert exact COM method names and positional argument order. No SolidWorks required.
- Every issue ends with `bash scripts/check.sh` exiting 0.

## Requirements
- Add `solidworks_mcp/version_gate.py`: read the connected version via `ISldWorks::RevisionNumber` (handling the property-vs-method ambiguity as `base.py` already does), parse it into a comparable release year/build, and expose `require_version(min_release)`.
- Add a `min_release` argument to the `@tool` decorator. `dispatch` checks it before invoking a handler and returns a clear, actionable error naming the connected version, the required version, and the tool - it must fail loudly, never fall back to a deprecated overload.
- Make the minimum release configurable in `solidworks_mcp/config.py` (default 2025) so the gate can be relaxed deliberately rather than by accident.
- Add a `get_capabilities()` tool returning the connected version, the minimum required version, and every registered tool with its `min_release` and whether it is currently usable. This is how an LLM discovers what it can do before it tries.
- Add `docs/TOOLS.md`, GENERATED by `scripts/gen_tools_doc.py` from the registry (name, description, parameters, min release, dossier reference). Wire a check into `scripts/check.sh` that regenerates it and fails if the committed file is out of date - so the docs cannot drift from the code.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Version parsing handles the real `RevisionNumber` string format (research and document it) plus the property-vs-method ambiguity
- [ ] A tool with `min_release=2025` dispatched against a simulated 2021 session returns a clear error naming both versions and the tool
- [ ] `get_capabilities()` lists every registered tool with its usability flag
- [ ] `docs/TOOLS.md` is generated and covers every registered tool
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh` fails when `docs/TOOLS.md` is stale (prove it in a test)
- [ ] `solidworks_mcp/tests/test_version_gate.py` has at least 10 tests
- [ ] `bash scripts/check.sh` passes

## Verification
```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest solidworks_mcp/tests/test_version_gate.py -q
.venv/bin/python scripts/gen_tools_doc.py --check
bash scripts/check.sh
```
